rule_hypotheses.rule: Base payout = sum of covered move-out charges the PM actually claimed (damage/repairs, painting, flooring wear, cleaning, carpet cleaning, trash-out, rekey, unpaid in-term or prorated rent, lease-break/re-rent fee) minus credits, capped at Max Benefit. Adjusters never add charges the PM did not claim (e.g. early move-out with no lease-break charge).
Exclude insurance/program add-ons billed on the ledger: renters insurance / RBP, SDRP or zero-deposit premiums, amenity service packages.
Exclude late fees and utilities (water bills).
Exclude flood/water damage caused by a tenant appliance such as a washing-machine flood; it belongs to renters insurance. Pay rekey and trash removal on the same claim.
Net credits on the move-out statement (prepaid or ledger credit balance) against covered charges.

Rent-based cap = rent rounded UP to the next $500 (1100 -> 1500). It applies only to policies written under the July 2023 program rules, i.e. SD addendum signed after about July 2023. Earlier policies are capped only by Max Benefit. 522 is ambiguous: ledger move-in is Jan 2024 but the sheet lease start is 2023-02-12.

When the PM submits a completed SDRP Move Out Form or calculation, the adjuster often pays the form total as-is, including maintenance coordination fees and un-itemized 'unpaid rent & fees', subject to caps.
Decline (0) when the sheet row has no Policy #, Treaty # or Max Benefit ('Not our policy').

If first month's rent was not collected before move-in, or the PM used the wrong premium rate table, the claim is normally declined or reduced. In 793 the adjuster instead paid a goodwill amount one band lower (1500 instead of the 2000 band). This exception cannot be computed from documents.
Claims from 2022 do not automatically pay Max Benefit: 23 paid the $225 invoiced against a 2500 max.

extraction_lessons: PURE Columbia 'Final Statement' is a full AppFolio-style tenant ledger in reverse chronological order with a running balance. The claim is the trailing balance, i.e. the 'Tenant Chargeback' rows posted after move-out (445, 506). Earlier chargebacks during the tenancy were already paid; ignore them. The JPG demand email repeats the balance.

Propertyware ledgers (Blue Fox 80, PURE Charleston 657, PURE AL 793) mark rows 'Unpaid Charge' vs 'Paid Charge'. Sum only the Unpaid rows. 'Partially Paid' late fees with later 'Charge Adjustment' rows must be netted (793). The Balance column is a running total, not a line amount.

The SDRP Move Out Calculation (657) can predate later ledger charges such as the next month's rent, premium and RBP. The ledger balance (2971) was higher than the calc (1790). Here the cap made the difference moot.
PURE's handwritten 'SDRP Move Out Form' (661) is scanned, so vision is needed. Its listed deductions and total are what the adjuster paid. Vendor invoices may not add up to the form lines.

Rent Manager statements (Johnson PM, 522) come as a 'full ledger' plus an 'updated final statement' that repeat the same post-move-out charges; use only one. The collection letter can carry a superseded total (2105.50, hand-updated to 2055.50 per dispute).

On Yardi-style Move Out Statements and SDI forms (Perry Reid, 881), the running balance starts negative (prepaid). The SDI nets the remaining credit (-3.00) into the amount due, and the adjuster paid the netted figure.
Blue Fox 'Statement of Accounting' (80) is an image-only PDF with vendor invoices and an envelope attached; read it with vision.
Some folders hold only a lease (978) or only a vendor invoice (23). Without an itemization, the approved amount cannot be rebuilt, so flag the claim as missing docs.

Sheet dates are unreliable. 445's move-out year is wrong (2024 vs 2023). 522's lease start and move-out don't match the ledger. 80's lease start differs from the ledger. Prefer document dates and keep sheet dates as fallbacks.

The workbook 'Comments' sheet keyed 'Row N' does NOT line up with tracking N-1. Comment dates fall before claim dates (Row 979 comments are from 08/2023 but claim 978 was filed 11/2024), and the content belongs to other claims (Row 882 approves $1,785, which equals 319's rent). Do not join it naively.

Ignore irrelevant docs: ACH/direct-deposit authorizations with bank data (881), long leases and SD addenda. Addenda are useful only for the waiver premium, the waived deposit amount and the signing date (relevant to the July-2023 rule era).
